outcome.technical: tools/reach-diff.py only. The exit is now ONE SHAPE, held by the AST walk plus settle at run time, with no literal-value enumeration left (_CODE_WRITERS, _ints, _code_values, _subscript_key, _EXIT_CALLS removed). R39 (med): main is `try: return settle(run(argv, out), out)` / `except KeyboardInterrupt: return settle(_interrupted(out), out)` / `except BaseException as exc: return settle(_unexpected(out, exc), out)`, so settle sits inside the guarded region and SystemExit (any argument) is refused as `internal` with its traceback. New main_shape() walk: every return is settle(...), the run is called once inside the try, no call before it, a handler catches BaseException, each branch returns. R40 (med): settle -> _unsupported() refuses as `internal` into a fresh result: a non-dict, a code that is not an int in 0/1/2 (bool excluded), a refusal not in REFUSALS, 2 with no refusal, a refusal with another code, 1 with no gap, 0 with a gap. R41 (med): the walk no longer reads values. It reports any name or attribute exit/_exit/quit/SystemExit outside the __main__ block, called or not, whatever its argument. In that block an exit must be handed main(...) or _selftest(). It also reports `import sys|os as X` and any `from sys|os import`. R42 (low): any Load of _refuse/_refusal/Refusal that is not a call's func goes to a new `bound` list. R43 (low): KeyboardInterrupt exits 2 under a new listed refusal `interrupted`. That was chosen over 130, which settle's {0,1,2} rule could not keep. Docstring: a new ONE PATH TO AN EXIT paragraph states what the walk enforces and, under WHAT IT CANNOT SEE, names: string-reached names (getattr/globals/__import__/importlib/exec/eval), signals/os.kill/os.abort, exits raised in other modules (caught by main at run time), and failures inside main's own handlers. The EXIT CODES 1 sentence now points at that exception. The [internal] entry is rewritten and [interrupted] added. Cases: rd64 widened (bound/exits/main clean on own source). rd67 repurposed to exit reachability (13 bodies incl. sys.exit(name), 1 + 1, True, `leave = sys.exit`, `from sys import exit as leave`, `import os as o`). Added rd73 (__main__ exit argument), rd74 (main shape, 5 mutations of main incl. variable-2 return and helper exit), rd75 (bound makers), rd76 (None/int result, SystemExit('x'), SystemExit(1) -> 2 internal), rd77 (never-listed refusal, code True with gaps, 3, '1', refusal with code 0, 0 with gaps -> 2 internal) and rd78 (KeyboardInterrupt -> 2 interrupted). quiet() now catches BaseException. Selftest 109/109. Mutation probe <scratchpad>/mirror/probe/mutations.py ran against a mirror copy, landed-assert each, purged __pycache__ and restored each mutation in the same run. 20 mutations: W1-W6 weaken the walk, E1-E7 are the reviewer's escapes written into the code (variable-2 return, sys.exit(1 + 1), sys.exit(True), from sys import exit as ex, import os as o, r = _refuse, settle moved out of the try), S1-S7 drop settle/handler checks (non-dict, never-listed, bool, refusal+other code, 0 with gap, no interrupt handler, handler narrowed). All 20 KILLED, 0 survived or not landed, probe exit 0, mirror cmp-identical after. The first probe run had W6 SURVIVE (rd73 held only non-call arguments), so rd73 gained `sys.exit(len(sys.argv))`. Two fixtures were tightened so each pins its own check: non-dict expects 'rather than a result', and code True carries gaps. Dependants: CONTRIBUTING.md:588-598 names the path, the command shape and --help, so it is still correct, with the CLI and flags unchanged. settle/parse_args/hook_line/total named elsewhere are same-name functions in other files, since reach-diff.py is hyphenated and imported by no one. settle(result, out) keeps its signature and still returns the exit code.
outcome.descriptive: reach-diff now has exactly one path to an exit, main -> settle inside a catch-all guard, held by an AST shape walk rather than a list of literal spellings, with settle refusing any result its exit cannot rest on and an interrupt refused as `interrupted`.
